_comment: Scout sources. Keys starting with _ are comments. Subreddit names go without r/. Tests validate this file.

comments._comment: Top-level comments of the most discussed Ask HN threads of the last few days, most-replied first. One request per thread.

reddit._comment: Must match the subreddits declared in the Reddit API access request (see README). Ask Reddit before adding more.

stackexchange._comment: API site names (softwarerecs = softwarerecs.stackexchange.com). Software Recommendations and Web Applications are mostly people asking whether a tool exists; the support sites (Super User, Ask Ubuntu, Apple, Android) and the niche sites after them (trades, hobbies, academia, work, home) only reach the Analyst with a pain phrase (export.dropWithoutPain). Money, law and health sites are left out: the compass rules out financial, legal and medical advice.

discourse._comment: Public Discourse forums, read through the JSON every Discourse site serves (/latest.json, /t/<id>.json; robots.txt only disallows search, RSS and user pages). name is the channel. maxTopics caps new topics per forum and run, each one a request. Check a forum's robots.txt and terms before adding it.

export._comment: Caps what the Analyst reads each week; this is what costs Claude usage.
export._questionChannels: Where people ask for tools or describe problems: ranked up by questionBoost (about two pain phrases' worth). "source" or "source:channel".
export._dropWithoutPain: Left out of the export unless they contain a pain phrase. Plain HN news is most of the volume and almost never a problem statement; Ask HN comments without one are mostly tool recommendations; the support and niche Stack Exchange sites and the forums are mostly one-off how-to questions.
export._contextSources: Launches and new projects: evidence of competition, not of pain, so they don't take the Analyst's slots. export --context-out writes them to a competition file that the Analyst and Critic search.
